title: The gate at Mukobeko stays shut: treason accused cut off from visitors as defence demands answers
excerpt: Prison officers in Kabwe have turned away visitors to Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused, according to people familiar with the attempts — the latest front in a case where procedure has become the story.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: 'Our diplomacy must help to grow Zambia': Haimbe works the UN corridors as two stories compete outside
excerpt: Two new diplomatic relationships, a Human Rights Council bid and a national statement on Monday — while diaspora organisers and the foreign minister tell different stories about protests at the gates.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'Two terms': the opposition is quoting Hichilema back at himself as the term-limits storm swirls
excerpt: State House has repeatedly denied any third-term ambition. But with Tayali's campaign growing louder and the President yet to address it directly this week, his own past words have become the opposition's favourite document.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The kwacha at 19.5, inflation at an eight-year low: a week of deadlines for Zambia's economic managers
excerpt: The currency has drifted softly this month while prices stay tame. Now three dates collide — the September inflation print, a monetary policy decision and the expiry of the fuel-tax moratorium.
author: Natasha Banda

title: KCM signs $498m deal to mine its own waste — the biggest tailings recovery plant in Africa
excerpt: Vedanta's Zambian unit will extract 70,000 tonnes of copper a year from decades of Chingola tailings, as the metal's price and the country's three-million-tonne ambition keep climbing.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Twenty-two games unbeaten: Belmadi's Algeria await the Chipolopolo in Tizi Ouzou
excerpt: George Lwandamina's first competitive match in charge is about as hard as African football gets — away to the Desert Foxes on Friday night, with Togo at home four days later.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Three wins, eight goals, one conceded: Junior Chipolopolo sweep Group C and meet the hosts on Friday
excerpt: A 3-1 win over Botswana sealed a perfect group stage in Maputo. One more win — against Mozambique in the semi-final — puts Zambia at the Under-20 AFCON in Ghana.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The season of the stage: Stanbic festival returns as Kwacha Music Awards locks in November
excerpt: Zambia's live-music calendar is stacking up — a bank-backed festival promising a star-studded local lineup, and the industry's biggest night set for 27 November.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: 'No cousin, no brother': Hichilema swears in his second-term cabinet with a warning
excerpt: President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn in the first batch of his new cabinet at State House, telling ministers that delivery — not relationships — will decide who keeps their seat.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

excerpt: A dispute has erupted over legal access at Mukobeko — while Harry Findlay's family says his health is deteriorating in detention.

excerpt: Days after urging the opposition to recognise President Hichilema and pursue dialogue, secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has been suspended.

excerpt: The Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance disputes the police account that Assistant Superintendent Daniel Banda took his own life.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kenya signs for 540,000 tonnes of Zambian maize — the record harvest finds its market
excerpt: The Food Reserve Agency has signed with Kenya's Baita Trading to export more than half a million tonnes of surplus maize.

excerpt: The disinflation run continues toward single digits. The market stall will confirm when it arrives.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Hichilema presses Vedanta to fast-track power investment as copper ambitions outrun the grid
excerpt: The president has urged Vedanta to accelerate power-generation plans, as fresh GreenCo funding signals the private build-out is moving.
author: Natasha Banda

excerpt: Suspected anthrax recorded in Muchinga Province; Lavushimanda reports no livestock cases. What the evidence says so far.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Barbra Banda nominated for the Ballon d'Or — again
excerpt: The Copper Queens and Orlando Pride striker is on the Ballon d'Or shortlist for another year.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

excerpt: Zambian champions Power Dynamos host Sudanese giants Al Merrikh needing to overturn a first-leg deficit.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Hichilema sworn in for a second term — and the economy is the whole speech
excerpt: Hakainde Hichilema took the oath at National Heroes Stadium on Tuesday after winning 61.4% of the vote. His promise for term two: investment, jobs, and three times the copper.

title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and Findlay moved to Mukobeko as treason case widens to 18
excerpt: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu and businessman Harry Findlay have been transferred to Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison on treason charges, according to multiple reports.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Zumani Zimba breaks ranks: 'Zambia must choose dialogue over division'
excerpt: Tonse Alliance secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has defied critics within his own camp to call for national dialogue — and even a government of national unity.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The kwacha is one of 2026's standout currencies. What does that buy you?
excerpt: Up roughly 20% against the dollar in a year and trading near 19.1 to the greenback, the kwacha is riding copper and a record maize harvest.

title: September 30 is copper day: the export-duty decision that reveals Zambia's real bottleneck
excerpt: Zambia extended its waiver on the 10% copper-concentrate export duty to the end of September while the country's biggest smelters sit in maintenance.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Zambia's copper boom runs on electricity the grid doesn't have yet
excerpt: Reaching 3 million tonnes of copper needs at least 2,000 extra megawatts. The power deficit was 707MW last year — but Kariba is recovering.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Fuel prices hold for September — and it's the suspended taxes doing the work
excerpt: Petrol stays at K25.29 and diesel at K26.86 despite Middle East pressure on oil prices.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Zesco Ndola Girls' COSAFA run ends in final defeat — 'we'll be back for the title'
excerpt: A perfect group stage, a semi-final statement, then Mamelodi Sundowns in the final. Zesco Ndola Girls fell short — but announced themselves.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Kangwa's Greek move and Lungu's injury race: the Chipolopolo European watch
excerpt: Klings Kangwa unveiled by Panathinaikos after a Hall of Fame farewell, while Gamphani Lungu races an injury before AFCON preparations.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Kopala showed up for Danny Kaya — and Lusaka got its turn this weekend
excerpt: The eighth Danny Kaya Music Festival packed the Copperbelt before a moving tribute to the late Dandy Krazy.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: Veteran Refinery shutdown: what is confirmed, what is claimed, and what remains unanswered
excerpt: The Copperbelt facility has halted operations under disputed circumstances. Allegations about the arrest of Mr. D. Nayek remain unverified.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Inflation falls to 6.5% — the lowest in eight years
excerpt: Zambia's annual inflation rate eased to 6.5% in June 2026, a level last seen in February 2018, as the kwacha firmed and debt restructuring steadied the economy.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Justice minister moves to defer Bill 7 again
excerpt: The Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Bill No. 7 was deferred once more in late June, with the Justice Ministry citing the need for further consultation on the divisive constitutional package.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema launches UPND manifesto: growth, jobs, free education
excerpt: President Hichilema formally launched his re-election platform on 11 June, promising continued economic recovery, expanded free education and support for agriculture.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kwacha touches 18 to the dollar — strongest in nearly three years
excerpt: The kwacha firmed to around K18.07 per US dollar in June, its strongest level since 2023, buoyed by copper earnings, reserves at about US$6.5 billion and renewed investor confidence.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema switches on Chisamba II: 100 more megawatts of solar
excerpt: The US$70 million second phase of the Chisamba solar plant was commissioned on 21 July, doubling the site to 200MW — a centrepiece of the drought-proofing energy push.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: The reserves row: US$6.5 billion in the bank, and a campaign over who feels it
excerpt: A debate over Zambia's record foreign-exchange reserves became the economic heart of the campaign, with Brian Mundubile asking what US$6.5 billion does for the cost of living — and Situmbeko Musokotwane answering.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: The burial that became a campaign: Lungu's legacy shadows the race
excerpt: A year after his death, the unresolved burial of former president Edgar Lungu has become one of the most emotive issues of the campaign, after Brian Mundubile promised a 'dignified burial' if elected.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Copper Queens wrap up pre-camp as preparations intensify
excerpt: Zambia's women's national team concluded a local pre-camp in July as the technical team steps up preparations, with attention on the next generation joining the Barbra Banda core.
author: Lusaka Brief Sports Desk

title: Election day: 8.7 million registered voters go to the polls
excerpt: Zambians voted on 13 August to choose a president, 226 constituency MPs, mayors and councillors — a vote framed as a referendum on the government's economic record.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema wins a second term with about 60% of the vote
excerpt: The Electoral Commission declared Hakainde Hichilema re-elected with about 60.5% of the vote against Brian Mundubile's 37.9%, while the UPND took a commanding parliamentary majority.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kabulonga operation: former minister Kafwaya killed, opposition figures detained
excerpt: A security operation at a Lusaka property days after the vote left former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya dead in what police described as an exchange of fire, and led to the detention of senior opposition figures — including, reportedly, Brian Mundubile found at the scene.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Inflation dips again to 6.2% — closing in on the target floor
excerpt: Annual inflation eased to 6.2% in August, a new eight-year low, with mealie meal prices falling month-on-month — welcome data for a re-elected government with promises to keep.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Lusaka rejects EU Parliament's post-election resolution as 'premature'
excerpt: The European Parliament has called for an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya and the post-election crackdown. Government says the resolution is premature and insufficiently informed.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others sue the State over their detention
excerpt: The eighteen treason suspects have petitioned over alleged rights violations, saying they were moved from Mukobeko to Mwembeshi without a lawful warrant — the first major legal counterattack since the charges were laid.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Mafinga South MP Faith Munthali critically ill after alleged abduction
excerpt: The newly elected MP is in Isoka General Hospital after what her family and party describe as an abduction. Police have been asked to investigate; details remain thin and contested.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mpundu accuses Tembo of betrayal as cracks widen in the Tonse Alliance
excerpt: Tonse Alliance chairman Binwell Mpundu has publicly accused Ezra Tembo of betraying those who built his career — the loudest rupture yet inside the opposition since the August defeat.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Former Education PS Henry Tukombe arrested over US$401 million contract
excerpt: Anti-corruption officers have arrested the former Ministry of Education permanent secretary in connection with a US$401 million contract — one of the largest figures ever attached to a Zambian graft case.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Honeybee case reopens: court clears DPP's appeal against Chilufya acquittal
excerpt: The Economic and Financial Crimes Court has ruled the Director of Public Prosecutions' appeal against the acquittal of former health minister Chitalu Chilufya in the Honeybee defective-drugs case can proceed.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Hichilema hosts the Duchess of Edinburgh as royal visit spotlights education
excerpt: President Hichilema met Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, during her visit to Zambia — a diplomatic bright spot in a month dominated by post-election tension.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mass anthrax vaccination targets 20,000 animals in Muchinga
excerpt: Government has launched a vaccination campaign covering 20,000 animals in Mpika, Shiwang'andu and Lavushimanda, with Mpika identified as the epicentre of the outbreak.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Daka double douses the Flames: Zambia 2-0 Malawi
excerpt: Substitute Billy Daka came off the bench to score twice in the closing stages as the Chipolopolo beat Malawi — a statement win in front of home fans.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Arrows stun Power Dynamos to lift the Charity Shield
excerpt: Red Arrows upset league champions Power Dynamos to win the season-opening Charity Shield — an early marker in what promises to be a fierce title race.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The term-limits storm: Tayali wants the ceiling scrapped — civil society says don't you dare
excerpt: Calls to scrap the presidential two-term limit have exploded into the open, with Chilufya Tayali leading the charge and civil society, opposition figures and a veteran constitutionalist warning of a third-term agenda.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Diaspora to protest at the UN as Haimbe arrives to defend Zambia's record
excerpt: Zambians in the US plan a demonstration outside UN headquarters in New York this week over the disputed election and the killing of Mutotwe Kafwaya — days before Foreign Minister Haimbe delivers Zambia's national statement.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Masebo challenges Chongwe East result over alleged malpractice
excerpt: Losing UPND candidate Sylvia Masebo has petitioned the Lusaka High Court over the Chongwe East parliamentary result — one of a string of election petitions now testing the 13 August outcomes.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 40 PR MPs sworn in as parliament widens — and watchdogs like what they see
excerpt: Speaker Nelly Mutti has sworn in the 40 proportional-representation members reserved for women, youth and persons with disabilities — the first fruit of the amended constitution's new architecture.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: More buyers eye Zambian maize as the record harvest goes to market
excerpt: Regional demand is lining up for Zambia's surplus maize weeks after the 540,000-tonne Kenya deal — with the FRA insisting food security is ring-fenced before exports move.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Lusaka, Copperbelt and Eastern top syphilis infections, health data shows
excerpt: New figures put the three most urbanised provinces at the top of the syphilis burden, with health officials urging testing and early treatment — especially in antenatal care.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Lungu and Liteta complete the squad as Chipolopolo eye Algeria
excerpt: Gamphani Lungu and Liteta have arrived in camp to complete the Chipolopolo squad for the Algeria clash, though German-based Andrew Sinkala has been excused by FAZ.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Haalubono handed the Copper Queens reins for the Olympic battle
excerpt: The Copper Queens have a new head coach as the federation turns its attention to the Olympic qualification campaign — a promotion from within for a programme that plans long cycles.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Short film, long shadow: Lusaka's festival wraps a breakout edition
excerpt: The Lusaka Short Film Festival has concluded after screenings that drew new audiences to Zambian storytelling — another marker for a film scene building real momentum.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk
